items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the function [MATH: f(x)] below:
[MATH: {3x^{2} + kx,|x < − 3,; x^{3},|x ≥ − 3]

Content:
The function [MATH: f(x)] seems to have a jump discontinuity at [MATH: x=-3.] However, by selecting a particular value for [MATH: k], we can remove the jump discontinuity and make the function continuous.

Content:
We can find this value of [MATH: k] by forcing the left and right-sided limits of the function to be equal at [MATH: x=-3\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \lim\limits_{x\to (-3)^-} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x\to (-3)^+} f(x)]

Content:
For the left limit, we have,
[MATH: lim_(x → (− 3)^{−})f(x)|= lim_(x → (− 3)^{−})(3x^{2} + kx); = 3(− 3)^{2} + k(− 3); = 27 − 3k,]

Content:
and for the right limit, we have
[MATH: lim_(x → (− 3)^{+})f(x)|= lim_(x → (− 3)^{+})x^{3}; = (− 3)^{3}; = − 27.]

Content:
Setting the left and right limits as equal, we have
[MATH: 27 − 3k|= − 27; 3k|= 54; k|= 18.]

Content:
Therefore, to make [MATH: f(x)] continuous at [MATH: x=-3,] we need to choose [MATH: k=18.]
